name: féith na filíochta

attributes.attribute: vein of poetry in the rear scalp
blood surged through the vein when composing

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The vein of poetry is an Irish folkloric motif. It was thought to sit at the back of a bard's scalp. When a bard began to compose, blood surged through the vein. It moved in the exact meter the poem required.

okr.objective: féith na filíochta is the vein of poetry in Irish folklore.
key_results: The vein of poetry is an Irish folkloric motif.
It sits in the rear scalp of bards.
When composing, a bard felt blood surge through it in the needed meter.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore
